text:
Nina: Heads-up — after the FP8 kernel rollout to canary pool we see ~0.7-1.2% request failures with NaN outputs. Happening on long-context traffic with heavy KV cache hits.

Mike: saw a few of these in SLO alerts earlier. NaNs come from attention softmax blowup? Any logs? :thinking_face:

Nina: Quick paste from one failing worker:
```
E/Runtime: fp8_kernel: scale overflow detected, output contains NaN at token 134
stack: aten::.. conv -> aten::softmax -> aten::mul
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.86 seq_len=2048 prefetched_tokens=1200
```

Carol: Interesting that kv_cache_hit_rate is high. That means we're stitching long effective sequences (cached + current) into one matmul path — exponent range spikes.

Jon: Rolling batching heuristics may be combining cached KV + new tokens into a single FP8 GEMM with no intermediate rescale. If scale * accumulated_value > FP8_max, we overflow -> NaN.

Mike: Reproducer notes: when we force kernel to INT8 or FP16, NaNs disappear but latency/regression changes. Perf-bot profiling summary:
```
perf-bot: 1836004601 - canary-fp8-pool
median latency +6% for fp8 vs int8 on short sequences
p99 spikes 2x when kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.7
kernel-switches: fp8_gemm_v2 fallback->fp16 in 14% of requests
```

Nina: So two linked issues: numeric overflow from fp8 scaling when context length accumulates, and kernel selector doesn't consider kv_cache_hit_rate or effective_seq_len distribution when choosing FP8.

Jon: I pushed a quick guard in runtime: detect kv_cache_hit_rate>0.6 -> force fp16 for attention matmul. Quick test on the canary reduced NaNs to 0.03% but latency regressed ~4% overall.

Carol: For a long-term fix we should: 1) implement dynamic per-GEMM rescale (pre-multiply by adaptive factor based on max_abs) 2) add smoothquant like per-channel scaling for linear layers during quantization calibration 3) update kernel selector policy to consider "effective_seq_len" histogram per route.

Mike: On smoothquant — remember smoothing per-channel reduces output dynamic range and helps avoid outliers. Calibration needs to capture KV-augmented sequences not just fresh sequence lengths. Our existing calibration runs use random prompts up to 512 tokens.

Nina: Agreed. We need a calibration corpus with warm-cache traces (simulate backfilled KV). I'll assemble a small set from prod-sampled traces (PII stripped).

Jon: Also observed another path: continuous batching with heterogeneous seq_lens causes internal scaling assumptions to break. If a batch contains very long-history item + short-history items, the long one dominates max_abs and we choose scale that crushes short ones into zeros -> quant noise and occasional denorm->Inf in subsequent ops.

Mike: Proposed short-term mitigations: 
- Add kernel-selector rule: if effective_seq_len > 1024 OR kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.5 -> prefer fp16/INT8 stochastic fallback.
- Instrument a per-request "numeric-risk" score and emit to console for routing decisions.
- Add a hotfix to rescale KV before feeding to FP8 GEMM: compute max_abs across KV chunk and apply safe_scale = min(scale, FP8_max / (max_abs + eps)).

Carol: Hotfix acceptable for canary but we must watch perf cost of extra max_abs reduction pass. Could be amortized with the existing KV pack step.

perf-bot: Canary telemetry after Jon's guard (FP16 for high-kv): NaN rate -> 0.03% (from 0.9%), median latency +3.9%, p99 unchanged.

Nina: Can we improve performance by using mixed path: keep FP8 for matmuls that only involve new tokens, and FP16 for matmuls that include cached KV? That reduces end-to-end latency while avoiding overflow.

Jon: That's doable if we split attention into two GEMMs: new_tokens x new_tokens (fp8) and new_tokens x KV (fp16). Need runtime change to pick kernel per-operand pair. Complexity: KV packing layout currently assumes single gemm path.

Mike: Sounds promising. Will add to RFC: "per-operand mixed-precision attention". Perf estimate: ~+1-2% median vs canary baseline, NaN mitigated.

Nina: For calibration changes: we should add a smoothquant pass to the quantizer that does per-channel absorb and scale clamping. Also expose a clipping threshold knob in the model profile so Optimize can recommend calibration params by workload.

Carol: Operational checklist before wide rollout: 
- Add per-route effective_seq_len histogram to console (7d retention).
- Update kernel-selector to consult histogram + kv hit rate.
- Add safe-scale precompute integrated into KV pack.
- Add calibration job that runs on warmed traces and stores per-layer scales.

Jon: I'll prototype split GEMM today and measure kernel latency. Mike you can work on the calibration + smoothquant impl. Nina can coordinate canary and create the prod-sampled trace set. Carol please add the console metrics.

Mike: One more note — we must ensure deterministic fallback ordering for A/B experiments so canary traffic doesn't silently see different numeric regimes. Add flags: `runtime.numeric_policy=prefer_fp8|prefer_fp16|auto-risk`

Nina: +1. Also add alert when NaN rate > 0.1% in 5m window.

infra-bot: Deploy plan recorded: canary patch branch "pr/4789-fp8-safeguards" -> 3-node canary -> monitor 2h -> auto-rollback NaNRate>0.1% or p99_lat_increase>1.5x.

Jon: OK starting prototype. Will post microbench numbers in this thread.

Mike: FYI, I ran a quick local smoothquant experiment — clipped L2 per-channel reduced max_abs by ~18% on average for layer_12 and layer_24 on our 13B baseline. Good signal that calibration will help.

Nina: Great work. Keep messages short — we want an actionable patch list and owner list for this week.

Carol: Owner list recap: Jon (split-GEMM + kernel-selector), Mike (smoothquant + calibration), Nina (canary traces + rollout), Carol (console + alerts).

perf-bot: Summary action items logged: [#1 kernel-selector rule], [#2 safe-scale KV pack], [#3 per-operand precision split], [#4 calibration with warmed traces].

Nina: Thanks team — will follow up with timeline and PR links. :thumbsup:
